reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the Nov 11 close (data fresh, not stale): SPX is 2.87% off its 120-day high at 7,619.38, 0.69% below its 50-day but 3.89% above its 200-day; SMH is 24.54% off its high at $506.96, sitting between zones just above Zone 2, while NVDA at $173.73 is below its Zone 2 floor of $175; VIX rolled over from a 28.18 five-day high to 17.49 and HY OAS is calm at 3.34, but the mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4 — zone occupancy and volume climax are both unconfirmed.
reaction.invalidation: A SPX close back above its 50-day average ($7,672.67) with SMH reclaiming Zone 1 ($540–565) and NVDA back above $185 would void the Watch stance — the correction would be over and the ladder's escalation rungs moot. Conversely, a credit break (HY OAS above 4%) voids the probe rungs entirely and the stance becomes stand-down, not Watch.

ladder.response: Prepare the Tranche A 25% probe only if the capitulation tally reaches 3 of 4 and VIX closes below 25 with HY OAS below 4% — the zone print alone is not a buy.
Treat as a bull trap: do not chase the bounce, do not add; entries wait for the retest verdict — a rejection at the failure zone confirms the pivot-and-fail and keeps the stance at Watch.
ladder.trigger: SPX or SMH bounces into the failure zone (SPX $7,750–7,820 / SMH $580–600) and stalls there

ladder.response: Stand down: the ladder's probe rungs are void, no new entries, and the deployment ladder's Tranche A/B conditions are re-audited from scratch.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 25, or HY OAS closes above 4%, or SPX closes below its 200-day average ($7,334.28)

ladder.response: Re-entry condition met: arm Tranche A (25% deployment) per the approved ladder, sized to the zone print, not to the bounce.
ladder.trigger: Fresh SMH Zone 2 print plus tally at 3 of 4 plus VIX below 25 plus credit calm (HY OAS below 4%)

reaction.trapRisk: NVDA is already below its Zone 2 floor and the live snapshot shows it down a further 6.03% today — the first bounce off these levels is the pivot-and-fail setup. Do not chase it: entries require either a fresh, confirmed Zone 2 print with the tally at 3 of 4, or a bounce that holds above the failure-zone retest (SMH $580–600). A bounce that stalls inside the failure zone is a short-the-rip zone, not an add, and any probe sized on the bounce alone is a trap entry.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is shallow at the index level (SPX 2.87% off its high, above its 200-day) but deep in the AI complex, NVDA has closed below its Zone 2 floor, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4 — no probe is armed and no add is justified until a fresh Zone 2 print arrives with confirmation.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the right read today, but concentration is the risk: the same divergence that reads as rotation becomes a rollover the moment credit flips. The index's calm is borrowed from a handful of names that are not falling — if HY OAS breaks above 4% or lending standards tighten, the 'rotation' label dies and the Mag 7 drawdown becomes the index drawdown.
themes.dataAnchor: The Mag 7 average sits 16.0% below its 52-week highs against SPY just 2.8% below its own high — a 13.2-point divergence gap — yet SPX is only 2.87% off its 120-day high (7,619.38 vs 7,844.52) and still 3.89% above its 200-day average. Credit agrees this is rotation: HY OAS is 3.34 and calm, and bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold. AAPL, the strongest Mag 7 name, is 0.1% off its high; NVDA, the weakest, is 28.6% off.
themes.label: Mag 7 rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as an AI-bubble unwind: the Mag 7 names that carried the index are down hard while the index itself barely moves, which the fear narrative treats as the start of a broad rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or SPX closing below its 200-day average ($7,334.28) — either flips rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: The gap between revenue growth and price is real, but it is not a free lunch: NVDA's decline reason is ACUTE_CATALYST, not pure sentiment, and an unresolved catalyst can keep multiple compression going while the overhang lasts. The opportunity is in names whose growth is confirmed and whose catalyst is priced, not in catching NVDA's falling knife below its zone floor.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue is still growing fast through the drawdown — NVDA +61.4% YoY, AVGO +55% YoY with a 67.8% gross margin and $26.9B of free cash flow, ONTO +41.5% YoY — while prices sit 28.6% (NVDA), 30.3% (AVGO) and 44.4% (ONTO) below their highs. SMH closed Nov 11 at $506.96, up 4.82% on the day but still 9.81% below its 50-day average; NVDA closed at $173.73, below its Zone 2 floor of $175, and the live snapshot shows it down a further 6.03% today.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of a falling price
themes.narrative: The market has decided the AI buildout is overpriced: NVDA is down 30.6% in a month, SMH is 24.5% off its high, and the complex is being sold as a bubble deflating.
themes.watchFor: NVDA closing back above $185 (top of Zone 2) versus a further close below $175 — the line between a zone test and a deeper washout.

themes.counterRead: Insider buying at the trough plus a 2.5x sales multiple is the strongest fundamental-vs-price gap on the board, but VST's decline reason is ACUTE_CATALYST and its revenue inflection is disputed in the data itself. Treat it as a screened candidate to verify thesis-first, not a confirmed bottom: the promotion's own revenue-inflection read is mixed, so the growth case needs verification before sizing.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the board's top conviction promotion (score 83) at $133.45, 29.5% below its peak, with a STRONG insider signal — insiders bought $1.17M at the trough — and revenue growing 19.1% YoY at a 2.5x price-to-sales ratio with $1,318M of free cash flow. The promotion flags its revenue inflection as STABLE_OR_DECLINING, so the growth read is not unanimous inside the data. BWXT, the adjacent nuclear supplier, is 48.0% below its high with revenue growing 18.3% YoY.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: trough with insider confirmation
themes.narrative: The nuclear power trade that rode the AI data-center story has been sold off with the rest of the complex — VST down 20.3% in a month, SMR down 22.0%, OKLO down 21.1%, GEV down 21.2%.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above $133 on a closing basis and any fresh insider filing; a close below $130 with no insider support voids the trough read.

themes.counterRead: DDOG is the cleanest version of this setup — growth, margins and cash flow all intact against a 38.7% drawdown — while NOW is the warning that not every software drawdown is a dislocation: its deteriorating revenue inflection means the price may be right. Screen name by name; the theme is real but the names are not interchangeable.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is the top conviction name (score 82, tier A) with revenue growing 27.7% YoY, an 80% gross margin and a 29.2% free-cash-flow margin, at an RSI of 31.5 and no earnings before Jan 14, 2027. NOW scores 60 at $102.76 with an RSI of 31, but its revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING — the one software name where the data agrees with the price. HUBS is 50.1% below its high at an RSI of 37.9 on a SENTIMENT_DRIVEN decline.
themes.label: Software / SaaS: growth stocks priced like distressed ones
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is being sold as if AI kills the SaaS model: DDOG down 38.7% from its high, NOW down 41.3%, HUBS down 50.1%, RDDT down 59.9%.
themes.watchFor: DDOG holding its tier-A conviction score on the next refresh and NOW's revenue inflection flipping from DETERIORATING before any software add.

themes.counterRead: There is nothing to be 'ahead of' here: price and narrative agree these vehicles fall when the underlying falls, and they fall faster. The risk is not missing a bottom but mistaking a mechanical levered bounce for one — TQQQ's 2.37% up day proves nothing about the next leg. No probe logic applies to this theme; it is a volatility warning, not an opportunity screen.
themes.dataAnchor: These are the deepest one-month declines in the tracked universe and they carry no earnings anchor to catch them — CONL at -52.04% and TQQQ at -26.53% are pure leverage working in reverse, and BMNR (a holding) is down 23.16% in a month. TQQQ bounced 2.37% today on QQQ's 0.88% gain, which is the mechanical 3x beta doing its job, not a bottom signal. IWM, by contrast, is up 1.7% over the same month — the washout is concentrated in leverage and crypto, not in small caps broadly.
themes.label: Leveraged and crypto complex: a washout with no earnings floor
themes.narrative: The leveraged and crypto complex is unwinding: CONL down 52.0% in a month, TQQQ down 26.5%, COIN down 28.4%, BTC down 10.9%, ETH down 15.8%, DOGE down 16.5%.
themes.watchFor: TQQQ closing below its November low on a QQQ down day would confirm the washout is still running; a QQQ close above its 50-day is the precondition for any levered re-entry discussion.
